plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding above value risks overpaying if I win against a high second bid; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. Since values are drawn independently and this is a one-shot round, I have no additional information about opponents beyond the uniform distribution, so truthful bidding remains optimal.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value ensures that if I win, I pay less than my value (positive profit), and if I lose, it's because someone valued it more than me, which is the efficient outcome. Bidding higher risks negative profit; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll stick to the theoretically optimal strategy of bidding my true value of $8.

This is a second-price auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy: if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding above my value risks paying more than the item is worth, while bidding below my value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, truthful bidding at $44 maximizes expected profit.
